description: BehaviorOS Knowledge Hierarchy — define a hierarquia de fontes de verdade, da mais confiável para a menos.

hierarchy.name: Repo
hierarchy.description: Estado atual do repositório — package.json, tsconfig.json, prisma/schema.prisma, source code.
hierarchy.useWhen: Always ground in this first. Repository state is the ultimate source of truth.

hierarchy.name: Architecture
hierarchy.description: Architectural decisions, ADRs, system design documents.
hierarchy.useWhen: Making design decisions, choosing patterns, understanding system boundaries.
antiPatterns: Never contradict established architecture without explicit justification

hierarchy.name: Versions
hierarchy.description: Precise version information from package.json files.
hierarchy.useWhen: Before any dependency-related decision. Always verify actual installed versions.

hierarchy.name: Official Docs
hierarchy.useWhen: When repository doesn't have the answer. Verify against official docs.
antiPatterns: Never rely on training data for library APIs
Never skip docs for less common features

hierarchy.name: Skills
hierarchy.description: Loaded skills with domain knowledge, patterns, and anti-patterns.
hierarchy.useWhen: Before implementing patterns, following conventions, or checking anti-patterns.
antiPatterns: Never skip skill loading for relevant file types

hierarchy.name: Patterns
hierarchy.description: Conventions, coding standards, and established patterns from the codebase.
antiPatterns: Never introduce new patterns without justification

hierarchy.name: Agent Knowledge
hierarchy.description: LLM's training knowledge — last resort when other sources fail.
hierarchy.useWhen: Only when repository, docs, and skills don't have the answer. Always verify.
antiPatterns: Never treat training knowledge as authoritative

hierarchy.name: Assumptions
hierarchy.description: Fallback assumptions — should NEVER be used for implementation.
hierarchy.useWhen: NEVER for implementation. Only for generating hypotheses to verify.
antiPatterns: NEVER implement based on assumptions alone

enforcement.requirement: Before implementing, agent MUST have evidence from at least Level 1-4.
blockingConditions: If only Level 7-8 evidence exists, BLOCK implementation
If no evidence from Level 1-5 exists, BLOCK implementation
If evidence contradicts, BLOCK and escalate
enforcement.note: Runtime-enforced (Knowledge Gate, oage-enforce.js PHASE 6d) for HIGH/CRITICAL risk operations only, adaptive per BehaviorOS governance philosophy — not a universal gate on every write. MEDIUM risk warns; LOW risk is off. Enforcement is scoped to the current sessionID (see policy-resolver.json 'knowledge-gate' and evidenceSourceMap below), not global across the whole audit trail. HIGH/CRITICAL are deliberately capped at level 3 (Repo/Architecture/Versions), NOT level 4 (Official Docs): level 4 alone would make this gate redundant with the context7-gate, which every HIGH/CRITICAL operation already requires (context7 evidence maps to level 4 — see evidenceSourceMap). Capping at 3 forces the distinct thing the hierarchy actually asks for: docs are necessary but not sufficient, the agent must also have grounded in the repo itself (Repo §1: 'the ultimate source of truth').

evidenceSourceMap.description: Maps the 'source' field recorded on 'grounding_evidence' audit events (oage-audit.js classifyEvidence) to a hierarchy level name above. Required because audit events use concrete source identifiers (which tool/file produced the evidence) while the hierarchy is expressed in abstract categories.
